newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish central bank logs March c/a deficit.
newsitem.headline: Danish central bank logs March c/a deficit.

text.p: A Danish central bank survey published on Tuesday showed a March current account deficit of 3.9 billion crowns, compared to a surplus of 10 million in March 1996, but economists saw no immediate grounds for concern.

Den Danske Bank chief economist Joergen Birger Christensen said that the central bank figures should be interpreted with care and added that the result might reflect the early occurrence of Easter in March this year.
"If the numbers do reflect a real trend it is worrying, but for the time being we should control our concern," he told Reuters.
National Statistics Office data, taken as the yardstick for most analysts, reported on Monday a higher-than-expected February current account surplus of 2.9 billion crowns.
The office will publish its version of the March figures on June 4.

Codan Bank's Niels Joergen Larsen agreed that the early Easter may have distorted the March picture and added that expected rises in pork exports should have a positive effect on the April and May current account figures.
The central bank data did not appear to worry the bond market, where benchmark prices were up around midday. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
